extracted.intended_audience: Authors submitting manuscripts to AEJ: Economic Policy (economics researchers)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for preparing and submitting research manuscripts to the American Economic Journal: Economic Policy, including formatting, disclosure, data/code, registration, and editorial policies specific to this journal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality / simultaneous submission prohibition
rubrics_metrics.description: All papers submitted to the AEJ: Economic Policy must represent original work and should fully reference and describe all prior work on the same subject. Papers under consideration for publication at another journal are ineligible for submission to the AEJ: Economic Policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For papers previously submitted to the American Economic Review or AER: Insights, special procedures are described later in the guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict of interest disclosure (personal/coeditor conflicts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior to submission, authors should familiarize themselves with how the AEJ: Economic Policy handles conflicts of interest between authors and coeditors. Potential personal conflicts should be identified in an accompanying cover letter during submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Editorial Policy linked on the site describes how conflicts are handled; identify potential personal conflicts in the cover letter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plagiarism screening / permission to check
rubrics_metrics.description: The AEA screens all submissions for plagiarism using CrossRef's Similarity Check. By submitting to an AEA journal, the author grants permission to the Association to check the manuscript for plagiarism using the Similarity Check system.

rubrics_metrics.name: AEA Disclosure Policy compliance (financial conflicts, IRB)
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions to the AEA journals should conform to the AEA Disclosure Policy, which provides principles for the disclosure of financial conflicts of interest and, when relevant, information regarding IRB approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclosure is author- and paper-specific; a specific relationship may be relevant for one of an author’s papers but not for another.

rubrics_metrics.name: Artificial intelligence usage disclosure and attribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Artificial intelligence (AI) software, such as chatbots or other large language models, may not be listed as an author. If AI software was used in the preparation of the manuscript, including drafting or editing text, this must be briefly described during the submission process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors are solely accountable for, and must thoroughly fact-check, outputs created with the help of AI software. The brief description helps editors understand how authors are or are not using chatbots or other forms of AI.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data, code, and computational detail for replication
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior to acceptance, authors of papers that contain empirical work, simulations, or experimental work must provide the data, code, and other details of the computations sufficient to permit replication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All submissions must comply with the AEA Data and Code Availability Policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: RCT registration for field experiments
rubrics_metrics.description: Research involving field experiments must be recorded in the AEA registry for randomized controlled trials (RCTs). (Laboratory experiments do not need to be registered at this time.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must supply the AEA RCT identification number during the manuscript submission process and should include a citation of their registration in the acknowledgement footnote of the paper. Sample citation provided: This RCT was registered as AEARCTR-0000005 (Zhang 2017).

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial discretion / right to reject without review
rubrics_metrics.description: The AEJ: Economic Policy reserves the right to reject any paper without review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Papers previously rejected by the AEJ: Economic Policy should not be resubmitted and will not reviewed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission fee policy and refund for desk rejects
rubrics_metrics.description: The AEJ: Economic Policy submission fee is adjusted according to AEA membership status and the economic classification that applies to the country in which the authors work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fee schedule: AEA members — high-income $200, middle-income $100, low-income $0; Nonmembers — high-income $300, middle-income $200, low-income $0. Papers rejected without review will be refunded 50 percent of the submission fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication fee for accepted papers
rubrics_metrics.description: If a paper is accepted for publication, a fee of $15 per typeset page will be assessed when page proofs are sent for author review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note applies to papers first submitted on or after February 1, 2024.

rubrics_metrics.name: Length recommendations and page-count conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: The average length of an AEJ: Economic Policy article is 33–34 typeset pages. We strongly recommend that manuscripts not exceed a length equivalent to 40 pages when formatted using 11-point font, 1.5 spacing, and 1-inch margins, or 45 pages when formatted using 12-point font, 1.5 spacing, and 1-inch margins.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The suggested length includes figures, tables, references, and appendices. Shorter, impactful papers will also be given full consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript file format requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: All manuscripts should be in PDF format.

rubrics_metrics.name: Style Guide adherence (optional at submission, required if accepted)
rubrics_metrics.description: Adherence to the journal's Style Guide is required for accepted articles but is optional at the time of submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title, byline, and author affiliations placement
rubrics_metrics.description: Title, byline, and author affiliations should appear on the first page of the manuscripts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract length requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: An abstract of 100 or fewer words is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: In-paper appendices: placement, typesetting, and page count
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscripts may include one or more in-paper appendices for technical proofs, derivations, and other material that can be separated from the main text but that is considered part of the paper. These appendices should begin on a new page following the text, preceding the references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In-paper appendices are typeset and edited and become a part of the total page count of the manuscript.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental Appendix: purpose and handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors may submit a Supplemental Appendix that contains material such as nonessential extensions, nonessential alternative specifications or robustness checks, and additional discussion that will be of interest to those pursuing work in the area.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supplemental appendices are posted under 'additional materials' and are not edited or typeset.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-contained paper requirement (essential information in main paper)
rubrics_metrics.description: The paper (including any in-paper appendices) must be self-contained, in the sense that a reader can understand and evaluate the findings without consulting the Supplemental Appendix.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All essential information, such as data sources, variable definitions, and methods (for empirical work) and proofs of the formal results (for theoretical work), must be included in the paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission channel and cover letter guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Once your submission materials have been prepared in accordance with these guidelines, please use the ScholarOne Manuscripts platform to submit your paper. A cover letter is not required and should only be used to provide substantive information, such as the identification of coeditors with whom the author may have a personal conflict of interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a cover letter is included, the journal prefers to receive it in the provided form field rather than as a separate document. Any data access limitations should also be noted in the cover letter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure Statement per author required
rubrics_metrics.description: Each (co)author should prepare a separate PDF document entitled 'Disclosure Statement,' which must be provided with the manuscript. The disclosure statement should include the (co)author’s name and the title of the article. If an author has nothing to disclose, that fact should be explicitly stated in the disclosure statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions that do not include these statements will be considered incomplete and will not be reviewed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of manuscripts previously submitted to AER / AER: Insights
rubrics_metrics.description: The AEJ: Economic Policy will consider papers previously reviewed by the American Economic Review or AER: Insights. In most cases, it is neither necessary nor recommended to revise the manuscript before submitting to AEJ: Economic Policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: During submission authors may request that the full correspondence files of the referees (including cover letters as well as referees' reports) be shared with the editors; the editorial staff will contact each referee to obtain permission. Guidance for response letters: for manuscripts identical to the AER/AER: Insights manuscript, submit a brief response letter (typically no more than 5 pages of text plus no more than 5 tables or figures) describing the main changes you would make; for manuscripts changed from the AER/AER: Insights manuscript, submit a response letter describing changes made and include response letters to the AER referees if changes were in response to them. Also upload the original AER/AER: Insights manuscript and choose file designation 'Misc. (for review).'

rubrics_metrics.name: Option to use AEA templates (review mode)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors have the option to use AEA Templates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If these templates are used, they should be used in 'review mode.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Preferred bibliographic style
rubrics_metrics.description: If you are using bibliographic software to prepare your reference list, we prefer that you use the 'Chicago Manual Author-Date' style.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joint paper author order option
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors may opt to publish joint papers in random order of coauthors using the symbol ⓡ between author names.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial contact information
rubrics_metrics.description: If you have any questions, please contact the AEJ: Economic Policy Editorial Office at aejinfo@aeapubs.org or call 412-432-2300.
